findings.desc: quality-cleanup: lifecycle-registry.ts has two identically-valued constants for the same concept: pre-existing COMMAND_LIFECYCLE_PHASES (line 52) and newly-added LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_PHASES (line 440) — both list the same 7 phases in the same order. No assertion in flow-stability-smoke.ts checks they remain equal, so a future phase addition to one but not the other will silently produce inconsistent contract checks: assertLifecycleRegistryConsistency() (line 859) uses COMMAND_LIFECYCLE_PHASES while assertPhaseFlowDerivedValuesByteIdentical() (line 963) uses LIFECYCLE_COMMAND_PHASES.

quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/core/lifecycle-registry.ts:332 exports `LifecycleArtifactRole` type but it is not referenced anywhere in the codebase — the contract test (lifecycle-registry-contract.ts:177) uses an inline `["produces", "consumes"] as const` literal instead. Dead export should be removed or actually imported.

quality-cleanup: packages/main/src/tasks/lifecycle-registry-contract.ts:141 uses `entry.name as never` to call `knownCommands.has()`. `entry.name` is typed as `string` (from the ProcessFactLevelEntry interface) and `knownCommands` is `Set<string>`, so `Set<string>.has(string)` requires no cast. The `as never` is an unnecessary type escape that bypasses type checking rather than a proper type annotation.
